name: Marjorie Taylor Greene
role: US Representative from Georgia (2021–January 2026); left the Republican Party in 2026
summary: A populist, hard-right Republican while in the House, she opposed abortion, gender-affirming care and gun control, and favoured immigration restriction and 'America First' limits on foreign spending and wars. From 2025 she broke with Trump on the Epstein files, Gaza, foreign wars, ACA subsidies, H-1B and AI preemption, and resigned in January 2026. Many standard policy questions (economy, institutions, constitutional design) are not covered by her recorded statements.

abortion-legal.rationale: Her official site states her number one policy goal is to end abortion in America; she cosponsored pro-life bills.

accelerate-technology.rationale: On AI she said 'We have no idea what AI will be capable of... giving it free rein... is potentially dangerous'; specific to AI.

close-ties-china.rationale: Urged colleagues 'Don't force us, don't force the American people, to rely on Communist China', calling China an enemy; she opposes reliance on it. The statement is framed as close ties with China instead of reliance on the United States; her remark opposes dependence on China, so -1.

corporate-influence.rationale: In her 60 Minutes interview (Dec 2025) she warned of being replaced by 'big pharma, big tech, military industrial war complex' and the 'elite donor class', and said crypto donors, big pharma and big donors were still getting everything they want.

decide-locally.rationale: On the AI moratorium she wrote 'We should be reducing federal power and preserving state power. Not the other way around.'

distribution-by-process.rationale: She defended older people’s wealth because they earned it and rejected attacking their ownership simply because they are wealthy.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Said 'no amount of taxes that anyone can pay is going to change the climate' and attacked the Green New Deal as forcing reliance on Communist China.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said on the House floor that 'every single one of us are equal. God created us equal and thank God we have a Constitution that affirms it.'

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: April 2023 post (as reported) called climate change a 'scam' and said 'fossil fuels are natural and amazing'; this praises fossil fuels but does not itself call for expanded production.

family-wage.rationale: Her own tweet described losing the ability to sustain a family and home on one income as a central national failure.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Attacked D.C.'s Local Residents Voting Rights Amendment Act: 'Local, you would think that would be United States of America residents, not noncitizens', and said it lets foreigners meddle in elections.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Introduced the Protect Children's Innocence Act (criminalising gender-affirming care for minors, passed House Dec 2025 per Wikipedia), filed amendments against the Equality Act, and said she refuses to recognise transgender women as women.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Said on the House floor 'God only creates two sexes and two genders, male and female' and 'God created us male and female', rejecting gender as a social construct.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Offered a censure resolution that treats the Holocaust as 'the genocide of millions of Jews' and condemns Tlaib for celebrating it.

limit-guns.rationale: Her official site says she is committed to defending and expanding Second Amendment rights; she introduced a bill to abolish the ATF and said the government will never tell her how many guns she can own.

more-religion-public.rationale: Described herself as a 'proud Christian nationalist' (reported); this comes from earlier years and her later stance on the label was not checked, so low.

nation-first.rationale: At CPAC 2021 said tax dollars 'should just go for America'; in 2025 told NBC she is a torchbearer of 'America First' and said Trump should focus on domestic affairs.

no-business-privileges.rationale: She said government should serve ordinary Americans rather than legislate favours for cryptocurrency, technology and pharmaceutical donors.

open-borders.rationale: Sought impeachment of DHS Secretary Mayorkas over border security (2023), sat on the Border Security subcommittee, and moved to end H-1B visas.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: In Nov 2025 she said she was 'not towing the party line' and not 'playing loyalty games'; she was removed from Freedom Caucus in 2023 and broke with leadership on the shutdown.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Told NBC the Trump campaign was a referendum on behalf of Americans 'so sick of Washington, D.C.'; said she opposes the 'elite donor class' and 'neocons' running the party; called Ukraine's government corrupt (reported).

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: She opposed public funding to remove any monument, explicitly including the contested Robert E. Lee statue.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: She defended historic monuments as national culture and condemned their removal as erasing American history.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Signed the discharge petition for the Epstein files and wrote 'Americans deserve transparency'; specific to those files rather than a general legal right.

public-service-media.rationale: As DOGE subcommittee chair she held a hearing against PBS and NPR, accusing them of using taxpayer funds to push radical left positions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Announced a bill to 'completely eliminate' the H-1B program (medical field phased out over a decade, no pathway to citizenship); earlier voted against the ALLIES Act and sought impeachment of Mayorkas over the border. She criticised mass roundups as unrealistic, but not lower levels.

religion-illusion.rationale: Told the House 'God created us male and female. In His image, He created us', speaking as a believer, which rejects religion as an illusion.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Told NBC in 2025: 'I don't see things through the party polls and the talking points; I look at the real problems and analyze them that way.'

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: At CPAC 2021 opposed foreign aid; introduced legislation to abolish USAID (shown on her official site); called for ending funding of Israel's Iron Dome.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Said on the House floor 'God only creates two sexes and two genders, male and female, and God does not make mistakes' and that no surgery or hormones can change that.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: She demanded that the president and his administration obey the law requiring disclosure of the Epstein files.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Reported as saying in 2021 she would impose strict tariffs on China; no broader statement on tariffs to protect domestic industry was found.

term-limits.rationale: She signed a pledge supporting limits of three House terms and two Senate terms.

notes:
Positions shifted in 2025: the most recent clear position was used. Earlier controversies (QAnon, 2018-19 posts, 'Jewish space lasers') were answered only where a statement's wording matched; she has said her earlier social-media posts did not represent her views and has disavowed QAnon. Wikipedia-sourced quotes are secondhand.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 13 answers taken from it, 17 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent full-list pass, no inference. Priority elective-rulers answered; other priority items lack statement-specific evidence. Calling for public engagement does not establish direct participatory decision-making; criticism of defence profiteering does not establish Marxist profit-exploitation doctrine. Her later national-divorce clarification retained legal union, so a general right to secede is not inferred. Older violence rhetoric is qualified by her later condemnation, yielding low-confidence mixed evidence. Recent tariff criticism concerns implementation and does not prove wholesale conversion to free trade. Her Nay on the bundled 2024 S.870 fire/nuclear bill was checked but does not identify opposition to nuclear expansion specifically. The FairTax bill’s initial text did not list her, and later sponsorship was not independently established, so no tax views were assigned from it. Full 2025 and 2026 interviews downloaded and all 490 statements checked. Main lane decides inclusion and legacy-list changes.

claude-sonnet-5-5 deepening pass (2026-11-01), from the local Congress corpus (House floor speeches, hearings, Voteview). Themes searched: death penalty, sentencing, conscription, police, nuclear, welfare and minimum wage, unions, Islam, equality, noncitizen voting, constitutional design, courts, federalism, ICC, Fed and money, regulation, tax, healthcare, farm and trade, civil service, China, NATO, immigration, race, religion. Most turned up only nearby cases (votes against Democratic bills, questions to witnesses, Ukraine and Israel funding) and were left null. Wikipedia-only answers were re-sourced to the Record or nulled. Review 2026-11-01 (integrator): quotes checked in the Record (H1339, H5409, H5992, H5086); close-ties-china lowered to -1 (thin).
